newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices little changed, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices little changed, trade thin.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices stayed little changed Monday despite further losses in crude, helped by strong natural gas prices and forecasts for colder East Coast weather later this week and next, sources said.

"I don't see why anyone would want to (aggressively) sell resid right now with gas where it is and winter coming," said one trader, noting strong gas prices over the last month have made resid the fuel of choice for utilities and industrials.
New York Harbor one percent firmed slightly to $21.25-50 a barrel on prospects for better utility interest. December one percent paper was talked slightly lower early at $21.25-50.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour notionally were little changed at $24.00 and $22.00-25, respectively.
High sulphurs in NYH also held steady, with 2.2 percent still at $20.25-50.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent edged up slightly to $18.75, while three percent was unchanged at $17.50-75.
No NYH or USG deals were reported.

New York City gate swing gas firmed more than 10 cents Monday to the $3.50s/mmBtu on forecasts for colder weather later this week and next. NYH one percent resid was at a $3.39/mmBtu equivalent. In December, New York gas was quoted at about $1.25-1.30 over the NYMEX screen, or about $4.25/mmBtu versus resid paper at a $3.39/mmBtu equivalent.
